title.narrative: Empowering young people with inflation-Resilient Livelihoods in Rular Damascus (PUSH+)

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project focuses on the economic empowerment of young individuals in Rural Damascus (Qudsaya) through a structured and strategic approach centered on comprehensive personal skills training, entrepreneurial development, and vocational training. Our program aims to enhance the economic resilience of youth, providing them with the tools and opportunities needed for sustainable growth and development.ltbrgtThe core activities of this project include intensive training programs designed to build personal and transferable skills essential for both entrepreneurial and vocational success. Recognizing the importance of entrepreneurship as a driver of economic growth, we will offer extensive training in small business management and entrepreneurship. This training will equip young participants with the knowledge and skills necessary to develop and scale their business entrepreneurship startup.ltbrgtIn addition to training, the project will provide substantial support for young entrepreneurs through small business grants. These grants will enable aspiring entrepreneurs to invest in essential resources and market assets, laying the foundation for successful and sustainable businesses. By fostering entrepreneurship, we aim to create high-income employment opportunities and stimulate local economic development.ltbrgtProject Activities:ltbrgt1. Training of 300 youth individuals on soft skills or transferable skills:ltbrgt - This training will include workshops on communication, leadership, and digital literacy, along with assessments to identify participants for subsequent tracks.ltbrgt2. Provision of Technical business and Vocational trainings for 150 youth individuals:ltbrgt - Beneficiaries will receive specialized training in high-demand sectors within the local market.ltbrgt3. Enrolment of 150 individuals in apprenticeship and On-Job Trainings:ltbrgt - These opportunities will be facilitated through partnerships with local businesses to ensure practical skill acquisition and increase long-term employment prospects.ltbrgt4. Support 50 people to start (or re-start) business entrepreneurship startup:ltbrgt - Business proposals will be reviewed by a specialized committee, selecting the best projects for financial and technical support.ltbrgt5. Provision of 30 support grants for existing MSMEs:ltbrgt - The needs of these enterprises will be assessed to facilitate business expansion and income enhancement, with financial support provided to ensure sustainability.ltbrgtImplementation Locations:ltbrgtRural Damascus (Qudsaya)ltbrgtTarget Distribution:ltbrgt100% in Rural Damascus (Qudsaya)ltbrgtTarget Group:ltbrgtReturning and affected youth, with a focus on reintegrating them into the economic process.ltbrgtImplementation:ltbrgtInitially, 300 youth will be trained in soft skills and transferable skills. The beneficiaries will then be divided into two main categories:ltbrgtCategory One:ltbrgt- Provision of Technical business and Vocational trainings for 150 youth individuals.ltbrgt- Enrolment of 150 individuals in apprenticeship and On-Job Trainings.ltbrgt- Provision of 30 support grants for existing MSMEs.ltbrgtCategory Twoltbrgt- 150 youth with business proposals and clear technical and financial studies will be trained in technical business and vocational skills.ltbrgt- Business proposals will be reviewed by a specialized committee.ltbrgt- Support 50 people to start business entrepreneurship startup.ltbrgtBy targeting these key areas, the project aims to foster sustainable economic growth and provide young individuals with the necessary skills and opportunities to thrive in a challenging economic environment.ltbrgtThis project complements prior interventions carried out by the foundation in Damascus or in other governorates, One prior project focusing on supporting MSMEs was carried out in partnership with Agha Khan foundation, "Scale Up Project" that supported 15 tech-based businesses with MSMEs grants, A project was also implemented with the International Labour Organization to provide on-the-job training for more than 150 young people and employ many of them.lt/pgt
